original_test_intent: Sustain the approved NVQual GPU and NVLink-switch system workload, then prove the platform remains usable with no defined bad-block condition, no new system errors and unchanged device/link/bandwidth health.
original_method: Pin NVQual/NVDiag build, module/config and expected roster; map GPUs/NVSwitches/topology; baseline link/bandwidth, memory/error, firmware, logs and telemetry; resolve duration and badblock oracle; isolate jobs and approve cooling/power/OOB; run tracked workload with watchdog and continuous telemetry; preserve full results; compare post-stress devices, links, bandwidth, errors and services.
manual_activity: Platform owner supplies harness/config, duration and badblock/link/bandwidth oracle; operator approves sustained load and recovery; agent may run the pinned monitored workload.

safety_requirements: Never translate badblock into a storage scan without an approved non-destructive oracle

engineer_actions: Resolve source conflicts and approve acceptance thresholds

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row273 Wistron-NV GPU-00266-V003: select four hours or 480 minutes, identify the exact NVQual/`./NV Diag` build/module/config and GPU/NVSwitch roster, define non-destructive badblock evidence, and approve per-link speed/width/bandwidth plus thermal/power/error thresholds and recovery.

review_improvement: Restores the actual system workload and turns vague health statements into topology-, telemetry- and oracle-backed evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: GPU and NVSwitch stress must overlap to exercise fabric traffic and shared power/thermal limits. A post-run log tail cannot show workload coverage or transient throttling. The term badblock could refer to GPU memory, harness diagnostics or storage; guessing a storage command risks destructive I/O and false coverage. Duration also matters because four versus eight hours changes both exposure and thermal soak.
